name: WHO Adult Triage: Obstructed Airway or Stridor at Rest
description: Any adult presenting with anatomical airway compromise or audible stridor at rest requires immediate emergency intervention.
section_number: Module 3: Airway and Breathing, Danger Signs

consequent.clinical_action: Immediate emergency airway intervention and ambulance activation (Call 112 / 108 / Resuscitation).
consequent.clinical_rationale: Stridor indicates critical upper airway narrowing that can progress to complete fatal occlusion rapidly.

name: WHO Adult Triage: Severe Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure
description: Adult oxygen saturation below 90% on room air constitutes an immediate life-threatening hypoxemia emergency.
section_number: Module 3: Airway and Breathing, Critical Oxygenation Thresholds

consequent.clinical_action: Immediate high-flow oxygen administration and emergency transfer to intensive care / emergency department.
consequent.clinical_rationale: SpO2 < 90% corresponds to PaO2 < 60 mmHg on the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve, indicating impending tissue hypoxia.

name: WHO Adult Triage: Profound Shock / Decompensated Hypotension
description: Adult systolic BP under 90 mmHg combined with altered peripheral perfusion is an immediate emergency override.
section_number: Module 3: Circulation, Signs of Shock in Adults

consequent.clinical_action: Immediate IV resuscitation, supine positioning, and emergency trauma/medical resuscitation team activation.
consequent.clinical_rationale: Hypotension with poor perfusion marks decompensated circulatory shock with imminent organ failure.

name: WHO Adult Triage: Unresponsive / Comatose (AVPU Scale U)
description: Patient unresponsiveness to verbal and painful stimuli indicates critical neurological compromise.

consequent.clinical_action: Immediate airway protection, recovery position if non-trauma, and emergency resuscitation alert.
consequent.clinical_rationale: An unresponsive patient loses airway protective reflexes (cough, gag) with severe aspiration and asphyxiation risk.
